# Current operating directive

**Updated:** 2026-07-08T02:46:00Z
**Author:** Jake (drafted by codex chat A9-A10, full-permission grant)
**Valid until:** until superseded

> Jake edits this file at any time during a work block. `codex corpus build
> --project specter_codex` rolls it into the cached prefix shared by every
> worker dispatched via `codex dispatch`. codex chat also auto-rebuilds the corpus

## Mission

Harden codex chat as the primary work surface and keep the whole stack inside
one $200 Max plan. Measured reality (2026-07-07): ~97% of Max burn is codex chat
foreground; workers are ~0 on Claude (gemini executors). The leverage stack:

1. **Prefix hygiene** — lean, current corpus (junk-gotcha filter, IRI dedupe,
   closed-plan exclusion shipped in kb_corpus.py); rebuild on staleness, never
   serve May-dated context.
2. **Cache discipline** — KB_CHAT_PERSIST_CLAUDE=1 everywhere; byte-stable
   system prompt per session; compaction folds (C1→C2→…) instead of verbatim
   replay; recall blocks bounded + flash-compressed on overflow.
3. **Usage visibility** — every LLM call site emits kb:UsageEvent (G1-G8
   complete); `codex tokens events` is the audit surface; instrumentation gaps
   (per-turn context breakdown, tool-calls-per-turn, cache-write reasons) are
   in-flight.
4. **Model throttling** — autorouter Sonnet floor, Opus/Fable on judgment
   signals, Haiku only via /allowHaiku; workers route by brief keywords
   (kb_dispatch_routing); gemini for synthesis/worker glue, never code.
5. **Multidev isolation** — per-(user,project) weaverd pools with identity
   gate (OS user, account, project) verified before execution (A5.79-83).

## Hard constraints

- **No-legacy.** Delete old code/graphs/repos/IRIs when superseded; do not
  alias / dual-write / keep-as-backup. The lone exception is PROV-O
  supersession arcs — those are the *why*, not legacy.
- **GraphDB-canonical writes only.** All knowledge writes go through `codex log`
  / `codex create` (or `codex capture` retrospective). No Markdown work-log appends.
- **No raw SPARQL into GraphDB from committed code.** Use `kb_sparql`
  helpers; add new helpers there if missing.
- **Monitoring is zero-LLM.** Never foreground-poll workers on an expensive
  model; `codex orchestrate --detach` + `/jobs` / `codex pipeline`.
- **Commit and push the moment work lands.** Git is the safety net; version
  bump (+0.01 minimum) in src/kb_chat/__init__.py on every codex chat change.
- **No emojis in code, commits, or docs unless Jake asks.**
- **Workers emit inline `codex log` atoms + final `outcome.json` + one-line
  stdout.** No Markdown reports from workers.

## Model preference

- **Foreground (codex chat):** autorouter default — Sonnet floor, Opus on
  architecture/judgment, Fable via pin. Gemini banned from foreground
  answers (compactor-internal use OK).
- **Workers:** `codex dispatch --llm auto` keyword-routes per KB_CHAT.md tier
  matrix. Gemini Cardinal Rule: code generation / mutation stays on Claude
  rwx tiers. Opus for design/decide-between/refactor/schema; Haiku for
  trivial; Sonnet mechanical baseline.
- **Reasoning:** Sonnet drift on ambiguous tasks costs more in retries than
  Opus correctness on the first pass.

## Approval scope

> **This section governs the FOREGROUND dispatcher (codex chat) — the decision
> whether to hand a brief to a worker at all. It does NOT govern a worker that
> has already received a brief. Workers must IGNORE this entire section: by the
> time work reaches a worker, the approval decision is already made. See
> "Worker execution mandate" below.**

- **Auto-dispatch:** yes, for in-scope worker briefs (no cross-project
  naming changes, no new top-level subcommands, no removing existing
  symbols without supersession).
- **Surface for review when:** new design decision, core-invariant refactor,
  CLAUDE.md / KB_CHAT.md doctrine edits, cross-project artifacts (site graphs,
  ontology files, bootstrap pipeline).
- **Never auto-dispatch:** pushes to remotes off the forge.tail515200.ts.net
  mesh; git-history deletion; subscription/billing surface changes.

## Worker execution mandate (workers read THIS, not Approval scope)

If you are an autonomous worker running a dispatched brief, you are the
authorized executor for that brief. The approval decision was already made by
the foreground before you were spawned — you have no one to ask.

- **Execute the brief. Do not defer, do not ask for confirmation, do not
  surface for review.** A run that ends by asking a clarifying question and
  exiting is a FAILED run, not a completed one — you exit into the void and the
  orchestrator false-greens it.
- **"Surface for review" / "ack before I write it" / "confirm the cwd" do NOT
  apply to you.** Your cwd, project, and scope are fixed by the dispatch. Ontology
  edits, TBox changes, and cross-project artifacts named in Approval scope are
  EXPECTED work for you when your brief says so — proceed.
- **If a genuine blocker stops you** (missing file, failing gate, contradictory
  instruction), do not silently exit 0: emit a `codex log failure` atom with the
  blocker, write `outcome.json` with `outcome: bailed` + the reason, and end
  with the one-line stdout summary. Exiting 0 with an unanswered question is
  never acceptable — it reads as success.
- **Acceptance:** a worker run with zero atoms emitted and no `outcome.json` is
  INCOMPLETE regardless of exit code.

## Drift escape hatch

- **Symptom:** 3+ null-result probes in a row without re-stepping back to the
  goal; next proposed step is another probe of the same shape.
- **Stuck >25 min (no commit, no atom-emit):** daemon flags the job; invoke
  the canonical reframe phrase: `review the items above and give better
  instructions`. The worker treats its own prior turns as input to evaluate,
  not commitments to defend.
